title: Loss Payee Services Bulletin: Notice Days on Deleting a Financed Vehicle from a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy
content:
A lender or lessor recorded as loss payee on a vehicle scheduled on a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy is owed notice when that vehicle comes off the policy. The loss payee notice days of a vehicle removal follow the removed vehicle's loss payee entries: the lienholder change entries recorded for that vehicle in the policy's transaction history, each marked as a new loan or a loan paid off.

## Rule

The first matching line decides:

| Removed vehicle's loss payee entries | Loss payee notice days |
|---|---|
| More new loans than loan payoffs recorded for the vehicle | 10 days: the notice owed to a loss payee whose interest is still open |
| The vehicle's latest loan payoff took effect after the credit start date | The calendar days from the credit start date to the payoff's effective date, at most 10: the lender's interest stayed covered until it was paid off |
| Otherwise (the latest payoff took effect on or before the credit start date, or no loan is recorded) | None: the lender's interest ended before the credit starts |

A payoff is placed by its effective date, whenever it was recorded.

## Cases (hypothetical, credit start date 1 April 2026)

| New loans | Payoffs | Latest payoff effective | Notice days |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | none | 10 |
| 2 | 1 | 1 March 2026 | 10 (more new loans than payoffs) |
| 1 | 1 | 5 April 2026 | 4 (1 to 5 April) |
| 1 | 1 | 20 April 2026 | 10 (19 days, held to at most 10) |
| 1 | 1 | 1 April 2026 | None (on the credit start date, not after it) |
| 1 | 1 | 15 March 2026 | None |
| 0 | 0 | none | None |
